Who I am

A chef shaped
by curiosity.

I hold a Master's in Data Science & Analytics from Royal Holloway, University of London — a background that gives me a unique analytical edge in the kitchen.

Since 2021 I've worked through incredible kitchens — from learning fundamentals as a commis chef to working alongside celebrity chef Giancarlo Caldesi at his AA Rosette restaurant in Bray.

I thrive under pressure, care deeply about hygiene and food safety, and believe the best dishes are born from both technique and heart.

My original recipes.

Three signature dishes — full ingredients, step-by-step method, and allergen notes.

Signature Dish

Scallops with Cauliflower
Purée & Dill Oil

A refined dish balancing delicate seared scallops with velvety cauliflower purée and vibrant dill oil.

3
Scallops
45
Mins
2
Servings

Ingredients

Cauliflower Purée

  • 1 small cauliflower
  • 2 cups water
  • 2 cups milk
  • 2 cups double cream
  • 1 tbsp salt & pepper
  • 2g thyme
  • 20g butter

Dill Oil

  • 100g fresh dill
  • 200ml cold-pressed rapeseed oil
  • 1 tbsp salt

Scallops

  • 3 scallops
  • 1 tbsp butter
  • Salt & pepper

🌿 Dairy Free Option

Use oat milk and margarine instead of milk, cream and butter.

Method

1

Make the Purée

Combine water, milk and cream in a deep pan. Bring to a boil, add chopped cauliflower, salt, pepper and thyme. Cook until soft. Drain, blend with 20g butter until silky smooth.

2

Make the Dill Oil

Blanch 100g dill in salted boiling water for 10 seconds. Plunge into ice water. Drain, blend with 200ml rapeseed oil. Strain through muslin into a squeeze bottle. Refrigerate.

3

Sear the Scallops

Heat oil until shimmering. Season scallops. Cook 2 minutes without moving. Flip, cook 1 min 30 sec. Add butter, baste 30 seconds. Do not overcook.

4

Plate & Serve

Swipe purée on a warm plate. Place scallops on top. Drizzle dill oil around. Serve immediately.

Signature Dish

Chicken Meatballs in
Rich White Gravy

Tender steamed and golden chicken meatballs in a smooth cashew cream gravy. Perfect with rice, naan, or pasta.

250g
Chicken Mince
60
Mins
3–4
Servings

Ingredients

Meatballs

  • 250g chicken mince
  • 3 tbsp plain flour
  • 1 tbsp black pepper
  • Salt to taste

White Gravy

  • ½ tsp cumin & coriander
  • ¼ tsp cinnamon
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 7 cashew nuts
  • 2 tbsp double cream
  • 2 medium onions
  • 1 tbsp fenugreek leaf
  • 1 green chilli (optional)
  • 1 tomato
  • 1 garlic clove, 2g ginger
  • Salt & pepper
  • 1 tbsp ghee or butter

🌿 Allergen Options

  • Gluten free: Use 2 eggs instead of flour
  • Nut free: Use pine nuts or extra cream
  • Dairy free: Swap cream for almond milk
  • Egg & gluten free: Steam only — binds naturally

Method

1

Make & Steam Meatballs

Mix mince, flour, pepper and salt. Shape into 18g balls. Steam 20 minutes. Cool. Reserve the steaming water for the gravy.

2

Lightly Fry

Deep fry cooled meatballs until just light golden. Drain and set aside.

3

Build the Gravy

Fry whole spices and nuts in 3 tbsp oil. Add garlic, ginger, onion and chilli. Caramelise on low heat. Add tomato, cook soft. Add 1 cup water, simmer 1 minute. Cool, blend smooth, strain.

4

Finish & Serve

Melt ghee, add strained gravy. Season. Add cream and fenugreek. Add meatballs, cook 2 minutes. Garnish with parsley and coriander. ✨ Add saffron for extra luxury.

Signature Dish

Pan-Fried Salmon with
Lemon Caper Butter Sauce

Crispy-skinned salmon finished in the oven, with a bright tangy lemon caper butter sauce. Under 30 minutes.

1
Salmon Fillet
25
Mins
1
Serving

Ingredients

Salmon

  • 1 salmon fillet
  • 4g thyme
  • 1 garlic clove
  • 2 tbsp oil, 15g butter
  • Salt & black pepper

Lemon Caper Sauce

  • ½ shallot, finely chopped
  • 1 small garlic clove
  • ¼ red chilli
  • 1 tbsp capers
  • 1 lemon — juice & zest
  • 30g butter
  • ¼ tsp plain flour
  • 1 tsp oil
  • ¼ tsp chopped parsley
  • Salt & pepper

💡 Chef's Tip

Sprinkle sea salt directly in the hot pan before adding salmon for extra crispy skin.

Method

1

Make the Sauce

Heat oil and butter. Add garlic, then shallots and chilli. Caramelise. Add capers, salt and pepper. Add lemon juice. Stir in flour mixed with a little water. Add 3 tbsp hot water to balance. Bring to one boil. Remove from heat, stir in parsley.

2

Season the Salmon

Pat dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

3

Pan-Fry for Crispy Skin

Sprinkle sea salt in hot pan. Place salmon skin-side down on low-medium heat. Add thyme and garlic. Add butter, baste top of fish continuously for 2 minutes.

4

Finish in the Oven

Transfer skin-side up on parchment-lined tray. Bake at 180°C for 4 minutes. Plate and spoon sauce generously over. Serve immediately.
